before.title: Demand pattern
before.body: Residence Inn demand follows market seasonality plus Bonvoy campaign calendars. Treat portfolio averages as directional only until property pace data exists.

before.title: Competitive pressure
before.body: Same-market Marriott sister brands can both help (Bonvoy shoppers) and cannibalize. Map sister-brand density before assuming exclusive Bonvoy capture for Residence Inn.

before.title: Conversion workstream
before.body: Systems, content, and rate integrity at cutover determine whether platform demand actually books the hotel in week one.

before.title: What is differentiated commercially
before.body: Extended-stay Marriott brand built for longer stays, residential kitchens, and weekly rhythms inside Marriott Bonvoy. Commercially, the brand case is Bonvoy + Marriott channels applied to a distinct Residence Inn product — not a generic Marriott International story.

before.title: Commercial engine
before.body: Residence Inn by Marriott sells through Marriott International distribution and Marriott Bonvoy while the brand product must still win the stay. Commercial diligence should separate platform reach from Residence Inn conversion on the property.

after.title: Commercial Engine
after.body: Residence Inn by Marriott commercial distribution rides Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and parent sales systems. Upscale extended-stay: full kitchens, residential suites, and Bonvoy for guests staying weeks with higher service and space expectations than midscale extended-stay. Owners should underwrite channel mix and loyalty contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.
